proposed_features.description: References to Apple-branded or Mac-specific hardware components (e.g., AppleTalk, PowerPort, Mac II, PB100) are more prevalent in one group, indicating a focus on Apple ecosystem.
Explicit mention of Mac OS versions (e.g., System 7.1) is a strong indicator of the Apple-centric group, as such references are rare in PC contexts.
Use of terms unique to Mac culture or hardware (e.g., Nubus, SIMM, PMMU, SCSI DB-25 interface) helps distinguish the group focused on Apple systems.
Mentions of Mac-specific software (e.g., MATLAB on Mac, DEC4015 terminal emulation, After Dark screensaver) are more common in one group.
Use of exclamation marks, emoticons, and enthusiastic language (e.g., 'FABULOUS setup !!!! :) Weeee!!!') is more frequent in one group, reflecting a passionate user community.
References to PC-specific hardware (e.g., Bondwell 38, 286, MasterCard for hardware purchase) are more common in the other group.
Mentions of OS/2 or DOS environments (e.g., 'operate under OS/2') are more typical of the PC group, as these were common PC operating systems.
Questions about PC-specific configuration (e.g., switch settings, identifying an old PC) are more common in the PC group.
Inclusion of ASCII schematics or circuit diagrams (e.g., for a DAC) is more common in one group, often associated with DIY or hardware tinkering.
References to file servers (e.g., Q700 file server) or network protocols (e.g., AppleTalk) help distinguish between groups, with AppleTalk being Mac-specific.
